run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-15T06:20:43Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is real and is driven by latency-induced client failures on two of frontend's gRPC dependencies, not by frontend itself. Frontend's STATUS_CODE_ERROR span share was 0 through 06:15:43Z, then 0.148% at 06:20:43Z, 4.74% at 06:25:43Z, 6.33% at 06:30:43Z and 3.66% at 06:35:43Z. The error spans are 407.68 each on GET /api/data, its route span and the client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, plus 79.3 each on POST /api/checkout, its route span and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder. Both paths start at about 06:20-06:21, immediately after deployments ad and payment were replaced by new ReplicaSets at 06:19:40Z / 06:19:39Z via a pod-template restartedAt annotation (identical image, env, ports and resource limits: a rollout restart, not a spec change), and neither deployment has readiness or liveness probes. After the restart the ad container consumed about 8x its previous CPU (0.0042 to 0.0347 cores), pinned at its 50m limit from 06:23-06:28, and was throttled in 89.9% of CFS periods versus 13.3% before; ad's GetAds server p95 went 113.6 ms to 15000 ms (10% of calls above 15 s) while its own handlers stayed fast (getAdsByCategory p95 1.90 ms) and it reported no ERROR status. Frontend's client-side GetAds p95 went 214.5 ms to 5700 ms, and the same pattern hit the payment path (checkout's Charge client p95 99.9 ms to 2811.8 ms, 76 client errors that ceased by about 06:25-06:27). The deepest driver of why the fresh ad container burned 8x CPU is not resolved: the current flagd-config ConfigMap has adFailure=on and paymentUnreachable=on (adHighCpu=off), which matches the two failing paths, but flag state during the window cannot be proven (no flagd logs, ConfigMap is current-state only, change_history is not integrated).

claims.text: Frontend's STATUS_CODE_ERROR span share (rate over 600 s) was 0 at the returned samples 06:00:43Z-06:15:43Z, then 0.148% at 06:20:43Z, 4.7417% at 06:25:43Z, 6.3345% at 06:30:43Z and 3.6557% at 06:35:43Z, matching the alert's 'current: 4.42' order of magnitude.

Frontend's STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in 05:20:43Z-06:39:42Z are concentrated in two dependency calls: 407.68 increase each on span GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds; 79.3 each on POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder; plus 15.25 on tcp.connect.

Both failing paths began at essentially the same time: frontend's GetAds error rate was 0 at 06:15:43Z, 0.007/s at 06:20:43Z, 0.467/s at 06:25:43Z and 0.696/s at 06:30:43Z; POST /api/checkout errors were 0, 0.0105/s, 0.137/s and 0.126/s at the same sample points.

Deployments ad and payment are at generation 2 and each gained a new ReplicaSet at the error onset: ad-5f8dd7c58d created 2026-11-15T06:19:40Z and payment-5d565cf9b created 2026-11-15T06:19:39Z, while the earlier ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 and payment-55766d76b9 are at 0 replicas; all other otel-demo deployments remain at generation 1.

The old and new ReplicaSet pod templates for ad and payment are identical (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and -payment, same env, containerPort 8080, same limits 50m CPU/450Mi and 20m CPU/160Mi, and readinessProbe/livenessProbe null in both), differing only by pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T06:19:40Z (ad) and 06:19:39Z (payment), i.e. a rollout restart rather than a configuration change.

Replacement pods ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 (created 06:19:40Z) and payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn (created 06:19:39Z) were Running and Ready with 0 restarts at query time, and Services ad/payment select opentelemetry.io/name with targetPort 8080 matching the containers' containerPort 8080, so the error paths are not explained by a service selector or port mismatch.

Ad's container CPU usage rose about 8x after the restart: old pod ad-554b849958-6z62j averaged 0.004170 cores over 05:19:00Z-06:19:00Z, while ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 averaged 0.034704 cores over 06:21:22Z-06:39:42Z; per minute it climbed from 0.0071 (06:21) to 0.0484-0.0491 cores (its 50m limit) from 06:23 to 06:28 and fell back to 0.0043 by 06:31.
CFS throttling jumped on the restarted pods: ad from 13.27% of periods throttled (05:19:00Z-06:19:00Z) to 89.87% (06:21:22Z-06:39:42Z), and payment from 13.78% to 34.10%.

Ad's own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server-span p95 latency went from 113.65 ms (05:19:00Z-06:19:00Z) to 15000 ms (06:21:22Z-06:39:42Z); the bucket distribution shifted from 965.6 of 1136.2 calls at <=10 ms with all calls <=800 ms, to only 26.8 of 149.3 calls at <=10 ms with 14.7 calls in the top (>15000 ms) bucket.

Frontend's client-side span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds p95 latency rose from 214.52 ms (05:19:00Z-06:19:00Z) to 5700 ms (06:21:22Z-06:39:42Z), so the latency is observed at the caller as well as at ad.

Ad's own internal work stayed fast and did not report failure: span getAdsByCategory p95 was 1.90 ms both before and after the restart, getRandomAds went 1.91 ms to 15.71 ms, and all 149.3 ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server spans in 06:21:22Z-06:39:42Z carry STATUS_CODE_UNSET with no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series.

On the payment path, checkout's client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge p95 rose from 99.92 ms (05:19:00Z-06:19:00Z) to 2811.76 ms (06:21:22Z-06:39:42Z), and checkout recorded 75.99 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on both oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, while service payment shows 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in the window and only UNSET Charge server spans (1133.27).

The payment-path errors were shorter-lived than the ad-path errors: checkout's Charge error rate was 0.265/s at 06:23:00Z and 0.263/s at 06:25:00Z and 0 at 06:27:00Z and later, while frontend's GetAds error rate was still 0.751/s at 06:27:00Z, 0.707/s at 06:29:00Z and 0.363/s at 06:31:00Z.
Frontend-proxy recorded its own STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in the window: 519.52 on operation ingress and 486.98 on operation router frontend egress.

The flagd-config ConfigMap (created 2026-11-15T05:46:52Z) currently carries demo.flagd.json with adFailure defaultVariant "on" and paymentUnreachable defaultVariant "on", while adHighCpu, adManualGc, paymentFailure, cartFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, productCatalogFailure, imageSlowLoad, emailMemoryLeak, kafkaQueueProblems and loadGeneratorFloodHomepage are "off".

Separately from the frontend alert, fraud-detection's container was OOMKilled with exit code 137, finishedAt 2026-11-15T06:21:26Z, and restarted at 06:21:27Z (restartCount 1); its only STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans are flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (1.02), none on operations involved in the frontend alert.

Leading explanation of the ad path: the pod replacement at 06:19:40Z put a container in place (with no readiness probe to hold traffic back) that consumed about 8x its previous CPU and was throttled in about 90% of CFS periods against its 50m limit in roughly 06:22-06:28, inflating ad GetAds server p95 to at least 15 s and frontend's client p95 to 5.7 s; frontend's GetAds client spans then recorded 407.68 ERROR spans, numerically equal to its GET /api/data and route ERROR spans (407.68 each), which is what lifted the frontend error rate to the alerting level.

Analogous explanation of the payment path: payment's replacement at 06:19:39Z produced a transient rise in Charge latency (checkout client p95 99.9 ms to 2811.8 ms) and 75.99 checkout client ERROR spans that ceased by about 06:25-06:27, producing frontend's 79.3 POST /api/checkout and PlaceOrder errors; the transience matches a warm-up or unavailability window of the new payment pod rather than a persistent fault.

An unresolved alternative or complementary cause is deliberate fault injection through flagd: the ConfigMap's current adFailure="on" and paymentUnreachable="on" match the two failing call paths (ad GetAds, checkout to payment Charge) exactly, and the ad/payment rollout restarts at 06:19:39-40Z look like a coordinated change; but no evidence in this Run shows the flag values or the actor during 06:20-06:39, so this remains unproven.

Ad was not rejecting GetAds with an error status: all 149.3 ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server spans after the restart carry STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series exists for that operation, so the frontend GetAds ERROR spans are not explained by ad returning gRPC errors; the observed ad-side symptom is latency, not error status.

The current paymentUnreachable="on" flag value is not by itself sufficient to explain the payment-path errors: checkout's Charge errors ceased at about 06:25-06:27 while the ConfigMap still reads "on" at query time (about 06:42Z), and payment's own Charge server spans remain present and UNSET throughout the window.

fraud-detection's OOMKill was considered as the cause and rejected for this alert: it occurred at 06:21:26Z, after the frontend error rate had already started rising at 06:20:43Z, its only ERROR spans are flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (1.02), and no fraud-detection operation appears in frontend's failing call paths (GetAds, PlaceOrder).

Raise the ad container's CPU limit/request (it is 50m; observed usage pinned at about 0.049 cores with 89.87% of CFS periods throttled) and add readiness/liveness probes to the ad and payment deployments, which currently have none, so a restarted pod does not receive traffic while it is still saturating its CPU quota.

Establish, with the change-history source that is not integrated in this Run, who or what ran the rollout restarts of deployments ad and payment at 06:19:40Z/06:19:39Z and whether flagd flags (adFailure, adHighCpu, paymentUnreachable) were toggled at that moment; this is the decisive fact for choosing between warm-up throttling and fault injection.

Restore diagnostic coverage for the failure window: the flagd and frontend containers produced no readable log lines in 06:10-06:39Z and Jaeger has no traces after about 06:04:16Z, so span-level error text for the 06:20-06:39Z failures was unavailable; retain log and trace history long enough to cover the alert window.

gaps: Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so who or what replaced the ad and payment pods (rollout restarts at 06:19:40Z / 06:19:39Z) and whether flagd flags were toggled at that time could not be established.

The flagd-config ConfigMap was read as current state (query at about 06:42Z); it is not historical, so adFailure="on" and paymentUnreachable="on" cannot be proven to have been the values during 06:20-06:39Z.

Jaeger returned no traces after about 06:04:16Z in this window: the traces_search view 0f6dfe50-da36-47d6-bf19-1d860a0030b8-t1:961bfb5b-e309-4a6e-a73c-eb3351113b0c for 06:22-06:39Z and the traces_search_by_tags view 60376954-544a-4365-9c3c-e360148b379a-t1:b4c8256a-a177-49b6-8c65-65c4aef433f5 for frontend operation grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds both returned no_data, as did 60376954-544a-4365-9c3c-e360148b379a-t0:b0ac5067-a7f1-4374-a0a7-6ec8a1d56f7d for frontend traces with error=true (c0c9a0b9-df78-45fa-8a29-597ebe85008a-t0:3c2a18af-1f87-44ba-aa5c-906fd6d067a6), so span-level error messages and gRPC status codes for the failing calls are unknown.

The flagd pod produced no log lines at all for 06:10-06:39Z (all six streams returned 0 lines) and the frontend pod returned 0 log lines for 06:20-06:39Z (views 68b1b1bb-418d-43e5-b4aa-1cb065136d6a-t2:22844377-1cb6-4de8-9903-5d6813175abf and 68b1b1bb-418d-43e5-b4aa-1cb065136d6a-t3:476e0c2d-6d85-4701-9680-a153fb6edbc6 returned no matching lines), so no application-level error text exists for the incident in the log source.

flagd exposes no traces_span_metrics_calls_total or duration series in the window (913cc560-aa53-40da-abf2-44561a5bad62-t0:9e4cd932-ca59-4cfd-9e3a-783328acf043 and 6969b75b-f684-49a9-a487-e4fc15bed48c-t2:3f6a8905-8159-47ad-8476-a3b4ca688c26 returned no_data), so flagd's own server-side flag-evaluation latency is unknown; only ad's client-side flagd spans were visible.

The rpc client duration query filtered to non-zero rpc_grpc_status_code (548c64a6-5c32-4d64-9ea6-e8756dcf5aae-t0:dde85b9b-787b-484b-b564-fb90103ff1b9) returned no_data, so client-side gRPC status code labels for these calls are unknown.

No Prometheus rule named RequestErrorRate was returned by list_prometheus_rules (1db46fb3-70b0-40fb-999f-6c51632f878b-t0:01a9109b-ee89-4f47-a11b-da8c28250bfa, status no_data), so the alert's exact expression, threshold and evaluation window could not be verified.

A pod-label query for app labels returned no_data (68b1b1bb-418d-43e5-b4aa-1cb065136d6a-t0:5db9abe4-0adf-4df0-a59d-afd21f3bebd6) and a non-Normal events query returned no_data (68b1b1bb-418d-43e5-b4aa-1cb065136d6a-t1:e793f4bf-afea-48f9-8cd2-cfa886c47bc1, event source window 06:19:39-06:21:27Z), so no Kubernetes events corroborate or contradict the rollout; the events view covers only its own timestamps.

The ad pod log read was limited to the newest lines (13a24d68-cd25-445e-a249-1c662dd1f005-t2:12fb9a23-7872-40cc-b7b1-ac978ad9035f is incomplete, newest 45 of 218 lines, read_through 06:29:27Z), so ad log lines before 06:28:59Z are unknown.
The cause of fraud-detection's OOMKill at 06:21:26Z and of its 63.54% CPU throttling after restart is unknown and not tied to this alert; it remains an unexplained change inside the window.

Services cart, currency, email, shipping, product-catalog, quote, kafka, image-provider and load-generator returned no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series for the window; absent series are unknown rather than zero, so these services were not verified healthy during the incident.

Whether the multi-second GetAds tail is confined to the 06:22-06:28Z CPU-saturation interval could not be resolved: the finest returned points for the latency queries were single whole-window values plus 5-minute error-rate points.
next_steps: Compare ad's post-restart CPU and latency behavior against a normal restart of a non-incident service to determine whether the about 8x CPU burst is an intrinsic cold-start effect of a 50m-limit container.
Ask the platform owner for the change record of the 06:19:39-40Z rollout restarts of ad and payment and of any flagd flag edits around that time.
If flagd is the suspected source, verify flag evaluation state at the time through flagd-ui or flagd audit output rather than the live ConfigMap snapshot.
Re-check ad GetAds p95 and throttling after raising ad's CPU limit to confirm the latency tail disappears.

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888
